title: Answer questions about an unfamiliar codebase
prompt:
This repo is fleetdesk, our fleet-operations API. I'm new to the codebase and need a few facts pinned down before an ops/security review. Please don't change any code; put your answers in answers.json at the repo root, in exactly this shape:

{
  "audit_writer": {"file": "<path relative to repo root>", "function": "<Class.method or function name>"},
  "webhook_backoff": {"config_key": "<key>", "default": <number>},
  "purge_expired_callers": ["<file path>:<qualified name>", ...],
  "unauthenticated_endpoint": {"method": "<HTTP method>", "path": "<full path>"},
  "duplicate_vin_status": <integer>
}

1. audit_writer: audit records end up in a database table. Which function actually executes the SQL statement that writes them? I want the function that issues the INSERT, not the generic database helper it calls.
2. webhook_backoff: outgoing webhook deliveries to customer endpoints are retried with exponential backoff. Which config key sets the initial delay, and what is its effective value (in that key's unit) when the service starts with no config file and no environment variables set?
3. purge_expired_callers: every function or method whose body directly calls `SessionRepository.purge_expired`, whatever the receiving variable happens to be called. Write each one as `<file path>:<qualified name>`, e.g. `fleetdesk/foo/bar.py:Baz.qux` or `fleetdesk/foo/bar.py:some_function`.
4. unauthenticated_endpoint: exactly one state-changing endpoint of the running app can be called with no credentials at all (no bearer token and no webhook signature) even though it isn't meant to be public. Which one? Give the HTTP method and the full request path as the app registers it, e.g. `/api/v1/things/{thing_id}/archive`.
5. duplicate_vin_status: the HTTP status code a client gets from `POST /api/v1/vehicles` when the VIN is already registered to another vehicle.

Answer from what the code actually does, not from names or comments.
